For God will testify against them, calling heaven and earth as witnesses, since He was about to rebuke Israel and make known to the angels in heaven and to the whole earth the ways of Israel's wickedness, so that no one would think that the beloved people, who had been chosen as His inheritance, were being rejected for no reason or for minor and insignificant transgressions. For God had pity on Israel as one who was being wronged, and He had freed them from the Egyptians' oppression through great power. But when the Egyptians retaliated, they were severely punished by God. Just as the reception of Israel was notable, so God wants the manner of their rejection to be known. If some people want to call the elements themselves to witness through the prophet's voice, the power of the thoughts would not miss the proper word, having been obscured. For Israel was redeemed from the Egyptians' wickedness through Moses. But when Pharaoh resisted God's signs and said, 'I do not know the Lord, and I will not let Israel go,' creation was armed against those who hated God, with many signs from heaven and on earth.

For heaven was pouring down hail, and earth was spewing forth frogs, as it is written; and the water was being turned into blood, and a furnace of burning coal was being kindled, and the air was being darkened, and sores and blisters were rising up on all bodies; thus, as it were, in vain the elements had toiled over those who had been redeemed; 'Hear, O heaven, and give ear, O earth, for the Lord has spoken'; we also apply ourselves otherwise to the notions of those who have gone before; for the Israelites, having despised the training through the law, and having neglected the teachings of salvation, and having left the one true God, were offering worship to unclean demons in mountains and hills, and in the most wooded valleys, and were sacrificing and prostrating themselves to the works of their own hands; and the God of all was grieving over these things, and very rightly so, and said to one of the holy prophets; 'Arise and plead your case before the mountains, and let the hills hear your voice'; 'Hear, O mountains, the judgment of the Lord, and you, O valleys, foundations of the earth, for the Lord has a case against his people'
pass_b_english: How could God tolerate the wicked deeds of Israel?

God will testify against them, calling heaven and earth as witnesses, because He is about to rebuke Israel and make known to the angels in heaven and to the whole earth the ways of Israel's wickedness, so that no one would think that the beloved people, who had been chosen as His inheritance and who possessed noble birth, were being rejected for no reason or for minor and insignificant transgressions.
For God had pity on Israel as one who was being wronged, and He had freed them from the Egyptians' oppression through great power.

But when the Egyptians retaliated, they were severely punished by God, who armed creation against those who hated Him with many signs, both many and marvelous, in heaven and on earth, including hail from heaven and frogs from the earth, as it is written (Exodus 7:19-8:2).
The water was also being turned into blood, and a furnace of burning coal was being kindled, and the air was being darkened, with sores and blisters rising up on the bodies of all people.
Just as the reception of Israel was notable, so God wants the manner of their rejection to be known.

If some people want to call the elements themselves to witness through the prophet's voice, the power of the proper meaning of the notions would not have been missed, though it had been obscured, for the elements had toiled in vain over those who had been redeemed.
For Israel was redeemed from the Egyptians' wickedness through Moses.
But when Pharaoh resisted God's signs and said, 'I do not know the Lord, and I will not let Israel go,' creation was armed against those who hated God.

The Israelites, having despised the training of the law and having neglected the teachings of salvation, and having left the one true God, were offering worship to unclean demons in mountains and hills, and in the most wooded valleys, sacrificing and prostrating themselves to the works of their own hands.
And the God of all was grieving over these things, and very rightly so.
He said to one of the holy prophets, 'Arise and plead your case before the mountains, and let the hills hear your voice' (Micah 6:1).
'Hear, O mountains, the judgment of the Lord, and you, O valleys, foundations of the earth, for the Lord has a case against His people' (Micah 6:2).
'Hear, O heaven, and give ear, O earth, for the Lord has spoken' (Isaiah 1:2).
